findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database will accept unencrypted client connections from the application tier, allowing credentials and catalog data to traverse the VPC in cleartext.

The instance user_data embeds the RDS master username and the password variable in cleartext, writing them into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the web app) and is visible in the EC2 console/API and Terraform state, leaking the database credentials.

The bootstrap installs and starts Apache serving the application over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration, so form submissions containing employee names and addresses and any session data traverse the network in cleartext.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a PHP application reachable from the network and an attached IAM instance profile, a server-side request forgery would allow an attacker to retrieve the role's temporary credentials from the metadata service.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the instance's root volume (which stores the generated dbinfo.inc containing database credentials) may be written unencrypted at rest.

The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the catalog database's storage, snapshots, and automated backups are stored unencrypted. Any compromise of the underlying storage or a shared snapshot exposes data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, removing the network boundary around the data tier and exposing it to credential-stuffing and exploitation attempts. Combined with the publicly exposed app server, this markedly enlarges attack surface.

The master password is supplied via var.password and the master username is hard-coded to the privileged default 'admin'; the password is passed in plaintext through Terraform variables and will be persisted in cleartext in Terraform state rather than sourced from Secrets Manager or managed via manage_master_user_password.

findings.issue_category: missing IAM authentication and audit logging
findings.description: The instance does not enable iam_database_authentication_enabled, cloudwatch log exports, or Performance Insights encryption controls, so database access relies solely on a static master password with no audit trail of connections or queries.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Because this role is attached to the internet-facing catalog_app_server via an instance profile, compromise of the instance (or SSRF against its metadata service) yields full control of all S3 buckets, EC2 resources, and RDS instances in the account, including privilege-escalation paths such as ec2:RunInstances with instance profiles and rds:ModifyDBInstance to reset the DB password.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control callbacks if the database host is compromised.

Neither the resource nor an associated parameter setting enforces TLS for client connections (e.g. require_secure_transport); combined with a public endpoint, database credentials and query data may traverse untrusted networks in cleartext.
